name: AL-06
label: Safe R

key_factors: Deeply Republican district (R+17 PVI) in Alabama
Incumbent Gary Palmer renominated and heavily outraising his opponent
Democrat Maurice Mercer raised only ~$6.5k with ~$1.9k on hand
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~3%
model.rationale: The baseline of R+17.4 is strongly supported by the district's partisan lean, Palmer's incumbency and financial dominance, and markets giving Democrats only a ~3% chance. With no polls or expert ratings suggesting otherwise, I stay essentially at the baseline with a slight nudge for the incumbent's resource advantage.
model.watch: A major scandal or unexpected incumbent retirement would be the only realistic path to moving this race toward competitive.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Alabama's 6th District is a solidly Republican seat, with a partisan lean of about 17 points toward the GOP. Incumbent Gary Palmer was renominated and enters the general election with a large financial edge, having raised over $1 million while Democrat Maurice Mercer has raised under $7,000 and has almost no cash on hand. No outside groups are spending against Palmer.

There are no public general-election polls or expert ratings for this race, so the forecast rests on fundamentals, which point to a comfortable Republican hold. Prediction markets similarly give Democrats only about a 3% chance. The expected outcome is a decisive Palmer victory, with any realistic upset requiring an unforeseen external shock.
